record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, can the general thermodynamic results of [13] be applied to determine the maximum entropy reduction these ratchets can achieve and to establish a full thermodynamic description of such systems?

evidence.quote: The application of the results of [13] to feedback controlled flashing ratchets has not been done yet.

It will allow to establish bounds on the entropy reduction attainable for feedback flashing ratchet and to establish the thermodynamics of these systems, which are theoretically and technologically relevant. Therefore, this is another relevant open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet, defined as follows. A Brownian particle (or an ensemble of non-interacting Brownian particles) of friction coefficient γ moves on the real line at temperature T, subject to thermal noise and to a spatially periodic, asymmetric (ratchet) potential V(x) which can be switched on or off. A controller measures the particle position at discrete times t_k = k·τ (k = 0, 1, 2, …) and, on the basis of the measurement outcome (and possibly the past history), chooses a control action α_k ∈ {on, off} that determines whether V is applied during the interval [t_k, t_{k+1}). The controlled stochastic dynamics is

   γ ẋ(t) = − α(t) V'(x(t)) + ξ(t),     ⟨ξ(t)ξ(t')⟩ = 2γ k_B T δ(t−t'),

with α(t) = α_k for t ∈ [t_k, t_{k+1}).

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics for systems coupled to a single heat bath and driven by a measurement-based feedback controller, an entropy balance of the general form

   ΔS_sys + ΔS_bath ≥ − I_fb

has been established, where ΔS_sys is the change of the Shannon/Gibbs entropy of the system, ΔS_bath the entropy change of the bath, and I_fb a non-negative information-theoretic functional of the joint statistics of measurements and trajectories that quantifies the information used by the controller.

Problem. Apply this general feedback-thermodynamic framework to the feedback-controlled flashing ratchet defined above to:

(a) derive an explicit, achievable upper bound on the entropy reduction
       R := −(ΔS_sys + ΔS_bath)
   attainable in a steady state (or per control cycle) by any feedback protocol α_k = F(x(t_0), …, x(t_k)), expressed in terms of the information functional I_fb associated with the position measurements and the parameters of V, T, γ, τ; and

(b) provide a complete thermodynamic description of the feedback flashing ratchet, i.e. identify the heat, work, system entropy, controller information, and their inequalities, so that the first and second laws (with the information correction term) close consistently for arbitrary measurement-based switching protocols.

Determine whether such a complete thermodynamic description and tight, attainable entropy-reduction bound can be obtained for the feedback flashing ratchet, and exhibit them.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has carried out substantial parts of this program: explicit upper bounds (linear in the controller's information) on the power output and on its gain over the optimal open-loop protocol have been derived for feedback flashing ratchets, an efficiency-at-maximum-power bound has been computed, and a Markovian description applicable to the feedback flashing ratchet, together with information equalities/inequalities and tighter information bounds on extractable work, has been developed. A fully closed, universally tight thermodynamic description with sharp attainable entropy-reduction bounds for arbitrary feedback protocols does not appear to have been definitively settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Information in feedback ratchets
status_evidence.snippet: Maximum power output upper bounded; upper bound for efficiency at maximum power; power-output gain over open-loop bounded linearly by information.
status_evidence.claim: Information-theoretic bounds on power and efficiency of feedback flashing ratchets have been established.

status_evidence.title: Efficiency at maximum power of a discrete feedback ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: Efficiency at maximum power computed for a discrete feedback ratchet model.
status_evidence.claim: Concrete thermodynamic performance bounds have been derived for discrete feedback ratchets.

status_evidence.title: Markovian description of a wide class of feedback-controlled systems: application to the feedback flashing ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: Markovian description applied specifically to the feedback flashing ratchet.
status_evidence.claim: A general feedback-thermodynamic framework has been applied to the feedback flashing ratchet.

status_evidence.title: Entropic balance with feedback control: information equalities and tight inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: New information bound for extractable work that is tighter and easier to evaluate than bounds based on the full control history.
status_evidence.claim: Tighter information-thermodynamic bounds relevant to feedback ratchets continue to be developed.
